title: OATH-Frames: Characterizing Online Attitudes Towards Homelessness with LLM Assistants

bias_targets.methodology: Developing a framing typology (OATH-Frames) to annotate large-scale social media discourse and comparing these frame predictions against existing sentiment and toxicity classifiers to evaluate how models capture subtle stereotyping and harmful rhetoric toward people experiencing homelessness (PEH).

Using statistical prevalence metrics (log-odds ratios) of specific framing annotations to measure differences in public attitudes and rhetoric when people experiencing homelessness are compared to other vulnerable populations, such as immigrants, asylum seekers, and Ukrainians.
